variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Apply the memory update before choosing the subgoal. Each episode starts with A: with the hand empty and remaining_targets nonempty, pick up the container identified by its first location. Point inside that container in the current image, using its visible center or another interior grasp point; small centroid shifts do not change identity. After execution shows a successful grasp and lift, the hand is holding a container. If remaining_targets is still nonempty, choose B to put down the held container before attempting the next target. After the release sequence leaves the hand open and empty, choose A at the first remaining target. A completed last requested pickup finishes the task; do not deliberately put that last container down as part of the goal. Do not infer an empty hand solely from stationary container detections: use the closing, lifting, and release observations. For an unexpected additional decision or an otherwise unmatched situation, choose B if the hand appears to hold a container; otherwise choose A at the closest visible container to the first remaining location. If that list is empty or no target can be located, choose B as the conservative menu fallback rather than inventing a new target.

fields.name: remaining_targets
fields.description: Initialize only when incoming memory is absent and the demonstration is shown. Associate each requested cube with the container placed over it. Within this demonstration-bearing decision, maintain a temporary identity-to-resting-position assignment for every container, giving unrequested and extra containers distinct temporary identities too. Initialize this assignment at the covering layout and process all subsequent movements chronologically, partitioning the demonstration into movement intervals bounded by settled layouts. For each interval, identify the departing resting positions from the visible intermediate motion, excluding stationary containers from the moving pair. This assignment is temporary computation, not an additional persistent memory field. Use continuous motion and direction through intermediate frames to assign endpoints; never reset identities at a resting layout or infer them from nearest original positions or detection-list order. Carry each identity along its intermediate trajectory through the final settling segment. For sparsely sampled curved motion, a change of direction does not itself mark another exchange: continue the same identity along that branch to its resting endpoint, rather than rematching the endpoint to an initial position. To resolve a curved exchange of two containers, identify the moving pair and exclude stationary containers from that pair's endpoint association. Estimate the pair's midpoint across successive frames and follow each identity's displacement around it. Assign the two settling endpoints jointly by continuing their observed rotational branches; do not assign an endpoint by proximity to that identity's starting position or by extrapolating only its last straight-line displacement. When the moving pair settles, commit both endpoint assignments before processing the next movement. Check each interval for exchange completion using the intermediate trajectories through settling. When they establish a completed exchange between two resting positions, jointly assign the identity previously at each departing position to the opposite resting endpoint, exactly once. Nearly identical unordered occupied positions before and after the interval do not negate this swap. Do not override the committed assignment by subsequently matching endpoints to initial positions. Keep every identity outside that moving pair at its committed position. Identify the participants in the next movement from visible departures and intermediate motion using this updated assignment, never the original cube-to-position association. Apply each later exchange to the current assignment, including exchanges involving extra containers or a different pair. After all movements have been processed, verify every requested identity's final assignment against the committed interval updates, including targets not selected by the current command and targets that exchanged with extra containers. For each requested identity, use its last committed endpoint, or its covering location if it never moved; later intervals in which it was stationary leave that endpoint unchanged. Then look up all requested identities in the final assignment to construct remaining_targets in goal order. Count a second exchange only when subsequent motion shows the pair exchanging endpoints again. A pair departing two resting positions and settling at the opposite endpoints completes one exchange. Neither the intermediate crossing nor the return of the unordered set of occupied positions counts as another exchange. Only a second complete exchange of that same pair restores its original assignment; exchanges involving a different pair do not cancel the first. Write the final container centers as an ordered list of [y, x] locations in goal order, including the target being selected now. Do not include unrequested containers in the list. An existing remaining_targets value of [] is completed memory, not absent memory, and must not trigger initialization. With existing memory, remove the first entry only when the execution frames shown at this decision show the hand descending to that target, closing around a container, and lifting with fingers still partly open around it. The observed successful grasps finish near 46% opening at raised height; unchanged reported container centers do not negate that grasp evidence. A release sequence, with descent followed by opening and withdrawal, leaves the list unchanged. Otherwise preserve the incoming list. Never remove an entry in anticipation of the command chosen now. e.g. [[121, 102]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of [y, x] container locations for requested pickups not yet completed. At the first decision, when the demonstration is shown and incoming memory is absent, associate each requested cube with the container placed over it. Follow each such container's identity along its entire moving trajectory through the demonstration, including exchanges with unrequested or extra containers, and list its final [y, x] location in goal order. Assign endpoints using continuous motion and direction through intermediate frames, not original cube positions, nearest-position matching, or detection order. A pair departing two resting positions and settling at the opposite endpoints completes one exchange, even though the unordered set of resting positions is unchanged. The intermediate crossing is not another exchange. Only a second complete exchange of the same pair restores that pair's original assignment; an exchange with a different container does not cancel the first. Independently track every requested identity through all movements; do not include unrequested containers in the output list. An existing empty list represents completed pickups and must not be reinitialized. At the decision immediately following a successful requested pickup, remove the first entry. Do not remove an entry merely because a pickup is selected at the current decision. Putting a container down leaves the list unchanged. Thus, at steps 2 and 3 of each two-target episode, the list contains only the second target. Locations identify containers rather than requiring exact pixel agreement. e.g. [[121, 102]]

history.critique:
field remaining_targets, POLICY PROMPT
  At initialization, the goals requested one hidden cube's container or two containers in color order. The moving containers finished near the same unordered set of positions they had occupied before moving. The policy treated some of these motions as identity restoration: it selected an original covering position instead of the exchanged destination, or selected the first target correctly but retained the wrong second destination. The intended memory instead listed the final positions of the tracked covering containers in goal order. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in demonstration-based initialization, also causing incorrect immediate or later target selection; it does not require another memory field or a change in subgoal rules. Strengthen the tracking instructions as follows: associate identities with containers when they cover the cubes, then follow each identity along its entire moving arc. A moving pair departing two resting positions and settling into those same two positions can constitute ONE exchange: the identities end at opposite endpoints. Do not count the intermediate crossing or the return of the unordered position set as an additional exchange. Use the direction of travel through the intermediate frames to assign endpoints, rather than resetting identities at each resting layout or matching only nearest positions. Only a second complete exchange of that same pair restores their original assignment; exchanges involving a different pair do not cancel the first. For example, a green-covering container moving [71, 123] → [73, 140] → [86, 158] → [103, 159] ends at [103, 159], even though another container ends near green's original position. The initialized value is therefore [[103, 159]]. In a two-target goal, independently follow both requested identities through all exchanges, including exchanges with unrequested or extra containers, and retain both final destinations in goal order. Replace the episode-specific initialization lookup with these observation-based instructions. Keep the field's meaning and subsequent updates unchanged: remaining_targets is the ordered list of final container locations for requested pickups not yet completed; initialize when the demonstration is shown with absent incoming memory, remove its first entry only when the currently shown execution contains the successful grasp and lift of that target, and preserve it during release. Selecting a pickup does not itself remove an entry, and an existing empty list is not a request to initialize again.

This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in initializing the identity-to-location list, leading to the wrong pickup despite the subgoal rule correctly selecting its first entry. Strengthen the existing continuous-motion instruction with an explicit sparse-trajectory example: green's path [97, 157] to [101, 144] to [95, 129] ends at [82, 131]; blue's path [81, 132] to [77, 145] to [82, 158] ends at [96, 157]. Keep the existing subsequent update rules: remove the first entry only after an observed successful pickup, preserve it through release, and never reinitialize an existing empty list.   During demonstration initialization, one goal requested green followed by red. Red exchanged places with an extra container, after which green exchanged twice with that extra container while red remained stationary. The policy correctly selected green first but wrote red's original location as the second target, rather than its post-exchange location. In another demonstration requesting red alone, red participated in the second of two exchanges involving different pairs; the policy selected red's original location instead of its exchanged endpoint. These are PREDICTABILITY failures in initializing remaining_targets; the single-target failure also produced the wrong subgoal. Make initialization operational by maintaining a temporary identity-to-resting-position assignment for all containers, including unrequested and extra containers. Identify the moving pair from the visible departures and intermediate motion, excluding stationary containers. When that motion settles after an exchange, swap the identities assigned to those two resting positions exactly once. Commit that assignment before interpreting the next movement. Determine subsequent moving identities from this updated assignment, never from the original cube-to-position association. A requested identity outside the next moving pair keeps its committed position. Two exchanges of the same pair restore that pair's assignment; two exchanges involving different pairs must be applied separately. Use the intermediate rotational trajectories to establish each completed exchange, rather than treating the return of the unordered resting layout as an identity reset. This temporary assignment is computation within the demonstration-bearing decision, not an additional persistent memory field. After processing all visible movements, remaining_targets still holds only the final [y, x] positions of requested containers in goal order; for example, [[81, 129], [129, 145]]. Initialize only with absent incoming memory and a visible demonstration. Preserve the existing later update rule: remove the first entry only after the currently shown execution confirms its successful pickup, not when selecting that pickup, and leave the list unchanged after release.
